item.itunes:summary:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WET8aARkNY8

值得閱讀的理由

  • 了解《Marathon》免費體驗週為何未能挽回玩家，反而引發伺服器、遊戲設計與商店定價等爭議。
  • 看見 Bungie 將資源轉向《Marathon》後，玩家對《天命2》的失望如何升高，甚至掀起要求推出《天命3》的連署。
  • 整理 Bungie 裁員、Sony 對即時服務遊戲的態度，以及《Marathon》未來可能轉為免費遊玩的傳聞。

摘要

《Marathon》推出後爭議不斷

作者指出，Sony 花費 36 億美元收購 Bungie，原本看重的是團隊經營即時服務遊戲的經驗。然而，《Marathon》上市前就被玩家拿來與《Concord》相提並論；推出後，遊戲又因美術與設計缺乏亮點、內容吸引力不足而遭受批評。即使 Steam 評價尚可，玩家人數仍持續下滑。Bungie 隨後宣布停止更新《天命2》，並傳出將更多資源投入《Marathon》，進一步激怒了玩家社群。

免費體驗週未能扭轉頹勢

《Marathon》第二季曾開放一週免費遊玩，並加入偏向 PvP 的模式、配對改善與機器人系統更新。玩家人數一度上升，但原因主要是免費活動，而非《天命2》停止更新後玩家無處可去。更糟的是，免費週首日便發生約十小時的伺服器故障，許多人無法登入；新內容反應平淡，資深高排名玩家還能取得較好的贊助裝備，讓新手更容易遭到碾壓。於是玩家數很快再度下滑，甚至落到《天命2》之下，Steam 好評率也受到新玩家負評影響。

第二季預告片同樣未能平息不滿。玩家認為影片過度著重 CGI 與氣氛營造，沒有呈現足以改變遊戲體驗的內容；有實況主還戲稱，玩家抵制只要一支三分鐘的電影預告就能結束，偏偏這支預告只有兩分鐘。與此同時，要求 Bungie 開發《天命3》的連署已超過四十萬人。

商店定價誤會與《天命2》回升

免費週期間，部分玩家在 PlayStation Store 看到《Marathon》豪華版只要 14 美元，並以為那就是遊戲本體的完整售價。實際上，由於他們已透過免費試玩取得本體，商店將帳號視為已擁有遊戲，因此 14 美元買到的只是豪華版升級；免費期結束後，若要繼續遊玩，仍須另購本體。玩家批評這種呈現方式具有誤導性，Sony 隨後更新商店資訊、移除該選項，並讓部分玩家申請退款。Bungie 也延長免費活動並提供遊戲內補償。

另一方面，《天命2》推出最後一次更新的當天，同時在線人數立即突破十萬，與《Marathon》免費活動的表現形成強烈對比。前 Bungie 社群經理認為，兩款遊戲面向的市場規模不同，不宜直接比較；他也表示，若玩家希望未來看到《天命3》等新作，現在支持《Marathon》或許有助工作室繼續開發。許多玩家與創作者則認為，要求玩家付費支持一款自己不想玩的遊戲，才能期待開發者推出想玩的作品，聽來既荒謬也沒有任何保證。

Bungie 裁員，Sony 仍看好即時服務遊戲

免費週前後，《Marathon》雖提供三成折扣，仍未能明顯拉回玩家。Bungie 在 6 月 25 日宣布大規模裁員；雖未公布人數，華盛頓州文件後來顯示約有 292 人受影響，工作室負責人也同時離職。公司坦承，《天命2》近年的表現不如預期，而其他新專案仍處於早期階段，因此必須縮減規模。玩家因此反駁，真正令人失望的不是《天命2》，而是 Bungie 的管理層。

裁員消息傳出後，《Marathon》每日同時在線人數逐漸跌入四位數，但 Sony 並未放棄即時服務策略，仍表示這類遊戲具有發展潛力。Sony 的財報則提到，第二季推出後，《Marathon》維持了高留存率，也持續吸引新玩家。作者指出，這種說法未必與總人數下滑矛盾：核心玩家可能留下，而免費活動帶來的新玩家也未必長期遊玩。Sony 並未宣稱總玩家數正在成長，或遊戲已達成原定目標；到了 9 月，《Marathon》同時在線人數已降至約兩千人。

免費遊玩傳聞與未明的前景

此外，網路上流傳 Bungie 正準備大幅改造《Marathon》，其中最受關注的傳聞是遊戲可能在 12 月改為免費遊玩。由於原定 9 月推出的第三季已延後至 12 月，有玩家猜測免費轉型可能會配合大型更新登場；不過，在正式消息公布前，這仍只是傳聞。影片最後提到，《Marathon》如今不只被拿來與 Bungie 自家的《天命2》比較，也開始與近期走紅的獨立遊戲 WDS 相提並論；原始字幕在此處中斷，未交代後續內容。

When a game announces the end of. support or development, it usually. means the title is nearing its death. However, some development teams choose. to bring games back via classic servers. so players can continue to play. But. Bungie recently made a rather different. move, directly targeting a game that. had already announced an end to updates. , attempting to revive it in another. way. What exactly happened? Hello. everyone, welcome back. A few months. ago, the game Marathon, developed by. Sony-owned studio Bungie, was mired in. controversy both before and after its. release. Since the official. announcement to stop updating the. beloved Destiny 2, the player community. has been further ignited. Bungie recently admitted that their. past decisions were a mistake and are. attempting to revive Destiny 2. What is. the current status of Marathon? And why. did Bungie suddenly turn back to pay. attention to Destiny 2? Next, Player. Confidential will share with you the. controversial events surrounding. Marathon. If there is anything I missed. or that players would like to add,. please feel free to leave a comment. below. Before we begin the video,. remember to like, subscribe to our. channel, and turn on the notification. bell so you don't miss any of our. updates. Sony spent $ 3.6 billion to. acquire Bungie, valuing their. experience in live-service games. Surprisingly, before Marathon was even. released, players were already mocking. it as another Concord. Although the. game sparked significant discussion. after launch, it faced controversy over. its visuals and design, while lacking. clear highlights. Its content and. long-term appeal were insufficient,. leading to a steady decline in. concurrent players despite decent. reviews on Steam. Later, Bungie. suddenly announced it would stop. updating Destiny 2, and it was even. revealed this was to pour more. resources into Marathon. This series of. moves further fueled the community's. outrage toward Bungie and Marathon. Player Confidential has already made. several videos sharing these events;

interested viewers can go check them. out. After Bungie stopped updating. Destiny 2 and shifted more resources to. Marathon, did the player count for. Marathon actually recover? Unexpectedly. , the player count did increase at the. time, but the reason wasn't because. players had nowhere else to go after. Destiny 2 ended support; it was because. the second season of Marathon was. opened for free for one week. This. season also introduced a PvP-oriented. game mode, matchmaking improvements,. and Bot system updates, leading many to. believe the developers are trying to. entice players to try the game before. deciding whether to buy the full. version. However, although many players. opened the game, a large number. couldn't even get in because, on the. first day of the free week, the game. suffered a server outage lasting about. 10 hours, preventing many from playing. normally. Furthermore, beyond the. lukewarm reception to the new content. and the lack of excitement for the new. PvP mode, media critics also blasted. the game's design, pointing out that. top-ranked veteran players get better. sponsor kits at the start of the season. , allowing them to crush newcomers with. superior gear and resources. As a. result, player numbers began to drop. again just days into the Marathon free. trial event, eventually falling even. behind the nearly dead Destiny 2. Players mocked the situation: "Even. when Marathon is free, the player count. is lower than Destiny 2's. It's. hopeless, bro. Even during the free. week, it couldn't even reach half of. the peak player count from three weeks. ago." Most awkwardly, not only did the. player count fall below Destiny 2, but. the 80%positive rating on Steam was. also negatively impacted, as many new. players left negative reviews after. trying the game during the free week. At the same time, the player community. launched a campaign demanding the. developers create Destiny 3, which has. now surpassed 400,000 signatures. Beyond the lack of appeal, the trailer. for Marathon’s second season was also. heavily criticized. Players felt it. focused too much on CGI and atmosphere. without showing what actual. game-changing content was coming. One. streamer joked, "I always say, every.

player boycott can be ended by just one. three-minute cinematic." Ironically,. this cinematic was only two minutes. long. The controversy surrounding the. free week didn't end there. During the. free trial, some players noticed the. Marathon Deluxe Edition on the. PlayStation Store was priced at just $. 14. Since the store page clearly stated. that the purchase included the base. game, they assumed $ 14 was the full. price and bought it immediately. In. reality, because these players already. had access via the free trial, the. PlayStation Store registered their. accounts as already owning the base. game, meaning the $ 14 was actually. just for the Deluxe Edition upgrade. In. other words, once the free trial ends,. players who spent $ 14 on the deluxe. edition during this period would. actually lose access to the base game. and would be required to purchase the. full version to keep playing. This. directly caused dissatisfaction among. many players, who criticized the game. for being deceptive. Sony quickly. updated the information on the. PlayStation Store, removed the $ 14. option, and allowed some players to. request refunds. On the other hand,. Bungie also took steps to address. previous server issues by extending the. free week event and providing in-game. compensation. As Destiny 2 received its. final update, the concurrent player. count immediately surpassed 100,000. that day. Despite both games receiving. updates during a free period, the stark. contrast between the two led players to. wonder if Sony and Bungie had backed. the wrong game. However, a former. Bungie community manager argued that. comparing Destiny 2's player count. directly to Marathon isn't entirely. fair, as Marathon is aimed at a smaller. niche market, while Destiny 2 is a. large-scale live-service game. He also. stated that for those hoping to see new. titles like Destiny 3 in the future,. supporting Marathon right now might be. a path that allows the studio to. continue developing. This sentiment. struck many players and content. creators as absurd, feeling like a. mockery that if you want Bungie to. develop a game you actually want to. play in the future, you have to pay to. support a game you don't want, even.

without any guarantee from the. developers. Although Marathon's free. week performance wasn't ideal, the. company didn't give up; they offered a. 30%discount during and around the end. of the free week to attract more. players, but the results failed to. bring back a significant player base. Subsequently, Bungie officially. announced large-scale layoffs on June. 25th. While the company did not. disclose the exact number, later. filings in Washington State revealed. that 292 people were affected, and even. the studio head, who had been in the. position for about a year, left the. company at the same time. Just as. players suspected these layoffs were. tied to Marathon's performance, the. company admitted in its announcement. that Destiny 2's performance over the. past few years had fallen short of. expectations, noting that after Destiny. 2's final update, new projects were. still in early development,. necessitating a reduction in company. size. Such a statement prompted players. to say "welcome home," noting that. Destiny 2 did not disappoint, but the. management at Bungie did. It’s over; Bungie can no longer stop the prophecy. of the "Cor" trilogy—this is Destiny. Following the news of layoffs, players. noticed Marathon's daily peak. concurrent player count gradually. dropping into the four digits, yet Sony. has not abandoned its live-service. strategy. The president of Sony. Interactive Entertainment still. believes live-service games have. potential, so they will continue to. pursue this field, aiming to build. online games with strong support,. constant updates, and lasting appeal. This statement has sparked further. backlash, as aside from a few successes. like Helldivers 2, Sony's other. live-service attempts have either. flopped or been unceremoniously. cancelled. Furthermore, Sony mentioned. in its financial report that with the. launch of Season 2, Marathon has. maintained a high player retention rate. while continuing to acquire new players. . This sounds dubious, but some point. out that even if total player counts. drop, high retention among core players. is still possible, and free weeks. attract many newcomers who don't.

necessarily stay long-term. Therefore,. a steady decline in concurrent players. does not directly prove that Sony's. claims of high retention are. necessarily false. However, Sony never. stated that Marathon's total player. count is growing, nor did they claim. the game is performing exceptionally. well or meeting its original targets. In other words, Sony may simply be. choosing to highlight positive metrics. like retention and new player. acquisition, even as Marathon's. concurrent players dipped to around. 2,000 by September. Additionally,. anonymous leaks have been circulating,. claiming Bungie is preparing a massive. overhaul for Marathon, with the most. notable rumor being a shift to. free-to-play in December. This is. considered plausible by some because. the third season, originally set for. September, was delayed to December,. leading players to suspect a. free-to-play transition might coincide. with this major update. Whether this. leak will actually come to fruition. remains to be seen until December. Now,. the game is not only being compared to. Bungie's own Destiny 2, but also to the. recent indie hit, WDS, which has sold. over 2.2 million units on PC,. generating roughly $ 70 million for its. developers. In contrast, Marathon was. launched simultaneously on multiple. platforms, but even so, WDS's total. accumulated revenue has already. surpassed Marathon's. Whether it was. making the second season free-to-play,. offering a 30%discount, announcing. layoffs, or the current rumors of a. future shift to free-to-play, Marathon. still hasn't been able to stop the. continuous loss of players. This makes. these moves look like a desperate. struggle to hold onto existing players. while trying to attract new ones. However, on September 22nd, players. seemed to see an unexpected turn from. Bungie. The head of the Bungie studio. and the general manager of Marathon. filmed a video admitting that Bungie. had indeed lost its way over the past. few years. They stated that the company. pursued its own vision too aggressively. without paying enough attention to what. players truly enjoyed, which led to. very real consequences, including a. loss of player trust and the departure.

of many talented employees. They also. acknowledged that the anger and. disappointment players feel toward. Bungie are understandable, as there. were many unfulfilled promises in the. past, and the company's priorities were. not truly centered on the players. Therefore, Bungie now intends to. rebuild player trust through concrete. actions, and the most important part of. this is Destiny. The two emphasized. that Bungie is definitely not done with. Destiny, and they will continue to tell. the Destiny story in the future. They. will also give the development team. more time to properly work on the. series, and the first step is bringing. back content from Destiny 2 that was. previously removed. As for Marathon,. they emphasized that it is not a game. meant to replace Destiny, but it. remains very important to the company's. future. Therefore, Bungie will make. major adjustments to the development. direction of Marathon. While retaining. the parts players currently enjoy, they. will also try to break through the. limitations of the originally set genre. . Once the news broke, players were. more concerned about Bungie’s. decision to revive Destiny than the. future of Marathon. Many players were. surprised and even delighted, saying. their hope was reignited: "Mom, I'll. call you back later, something magical. is happening!""Bro, as soon as he. opened his mouth, he said they would. bring back the Destiny 2 campaign. content; my heart skipped a beat right. then and there." However, some also. believe that over the past period,. Bungie kept making players feel like. Destiny had been abandoned, especially. after layoffs saw a large amount of. remaining resources poured into. Marathon. Yet, only about half a year. later, Bungie is telling players again. that Destiny remains the company's core. . As a result, they have begun to. question how much time and resources. Bungie has wasted, and how much more. manpower and capital will be needed now. if they are to reinvest in both Destiny. and Marathon simultaneously. Well-known. streamer Aztecross also believes that " Bungie" is only bringing up Destiny. again now not because they’ve. succeeded in listening to players, but. because Marathon’s poor performance.

has forced them to pivot their. development direction. At the same time. , he warns players not to get too. excited about the revival of Destiny. too soon, and even more so, not to. trust "Bungie" again. He argues that. they haven't suddenly rediscovered. their original creative spirit, but are. instead being swayed by commercial. realities, forced away from their. initial creative vision toward. practices that better serve the company. and its shareholders. I think that for. any Destiny player, if you're a Destiny. player right now, you are probably. happy. And I want to let you know that. you're wrong. You're wrong to be happy. You should not be happy right now. What. they're doing is they are being dragged. , kicking and screaming, away from. their quote "creative vision" into. what's called creating shareholder. value. >> Many players have also sarcastically. remarked that we’ve learned nothing,. and we'll be proven right very soon—. remember, their apology is purely. because they’ve run out of options; " we are so sorry." We are deeply sorry. We are sorry. >> The series of controversies surrounding. Marathon, from before its release to. after, not only impacted the game’s. reputation but the game's content also. failed to retain a large player base. That is why Bungie rolled out various. measures like updates, a free-to-play. week, and a 30%discount, hoping to. retain veteran players while attracting. more new ones. As it turned out, the. free-to-play week was plagued by server. failures, store pricing controversies,. and various content issues, which not. only failed to increase the player. count but actually increased the. negative feedback. Although the. official statement didn't explicitly. say that Marathon’s poor performance. was the reason Bungie was forced to. refocus on Destiny, the news of. Destiny's revival has certainly made. many players happy. As for whether. Bungie can actually regain player trust. through real action as they’ve. claimed, we’ll just have to see if. they can truly deliver on their. promises. 摘要

充滿爭議的配音員 Erika Ishii 與玩家反彈

作者指出，配音員 Erika Ishii 近年參與包括《羊蹄山戰鬼》等 3A 大作的英文配音，然而她的聲線表現與公眾形象卻在玩家社群中引發巨大爭議。除了過往在 LGBTQ+、反法西斯等議題上的激進政治表態，以及公開呼籲抵制《霍格華茲的傳承》外，她平時誇張怪異的肢體動作與網路迷因，皆讓不少玩家對其感到強烈反感。

摘要

Hermen Hulst 上任與服務型遊戲策略

作者指出，索尼互動娛樂工作室業務執行長 Hermen Hulst 因推動《星鳴特攻》、關閉工作室等決策，遭到玩家、媒體與業界人士質疑。前全球工作室總裁吉田修平曾參與催生多款主機作品，也支持《劍星》等遊戲；他在 2019 年卸任後，由 Hulst 接掌相關業務。作者認為，Hulst 的策略與管理方式引發外界對其領導能力的批評。

服務型遊戲計畫受挫

作者回顧索尼曾計畫在 2026 年前推出十多款服務型遊戲，並投入資金收購 Bungie，希望借重其營運經驗。然而，《星鳴特攻》上市僅兩週便停服，開發工作室隨後關閉；《最後生還者》、《蜘蛛人》等線上服務型遊戲計畫也遭取消。Bungie 自身則經歷裁員與延期，新作《馬拉松》的表現亦未達預期，令《天命》玩家不滿。吉田修平曾表示，自己對盲目追逐服務型遊戲抱持疑慮，這可能是其遭撤換的原因之一。

PC 發行與主機獨佔的拉鋸

Hulst 曾推動 PlayStation 獨佔遊戲移植至 PC，並規劃服務型遊戲同步登上 PC 與 PS5、單人作品則先在 PS5 發行。不過，作者提到索尼後來因考量 PC 銷售表現及主機吸引力，確認大型單人遊戲將回歸主機獨佔。索尼計畫停產實體光碟的消息也引起爭議，吉田修平為此辯護時遭玩家反彈，之後又以「借出空氣」的方式重現相關迷因。

工作室決策與玩家反彈

作者指出，索尼關閉推出《惡魔靈魂》重製版的 Bluepoint Games，並終止與小島秀夫合作的《Physint》，使 Hulst 的工作室管理決策再受批評。小島秀夫曾透露，合作案遭取消時，他一度擔心工作室無以為繼；影片稱該作後來獲 Xbox 支援，得以繼續開發。另一方面，Bungie 表示將重新聚焦《天命 2》，並逐步恢復先前移除的內容。PlayStation 與 BLACKPINK 成員 Lisa 推出限量手把，也被玩家拿來調侃其周邊款式似乎比獨佔遊戲還多。

策略爭議與下台呼聲

作者最後總結，Hulst 上任後推動服務型遊戲、調整獨佔策略並關閉多間工作室，相關決定接連引發玩家不滿。影片將這些事件串連起來，呈現 PlayStation 在商業方向與玩家期待之間的衝突，也說明為何有人呼籲 Hulst 下台。
